title: How to Add Zooms to Your Screen Recording After You Record
summary: How to add automatic zooms to a screen recording after you've recorded it: generate zooms from your clicks, pick a style, fix the ones you don't like, add motion blur, and share a hosted link without re-recording.
body_markdown:
You don't zoom while you record. Record the screen as normal, open the video in the[Tella editor](https://www.tella.com/editor) , click **Effect** , then **Generate zooms** . Tella uses the clicks and cursor movement it captured during the recording to put a zoom on each piece of action. Pick a style, fix the ones you'd have placed differently, turn on motion blur, and share the link.


Below: what Auto Zoom needs from the recording, how the styles differ, and how to clean up what it generates.


## Why zooms are added after recording


Older screen recorders zoomed live. You held a key, dragged the view, and the zoom was baked into the footage. To change it, you recorded again.


Tella captures the screen at full resolution and stores the cursor position and every click as data next to it. Zooms are computed from that data in the editor. Because a zoom is an effect on top of the footage, you can move it, resize it, delete it, or change your mind a week later. That's how[Auto Zoom](https://www.tella.com/screen-effects) works, and why nothing below involves recording twice.


## What you need


Auto Zoom needs cursor and click data, so the recording has to come from a source that captures it:


- **Tella for Mac** and **Tella for Windows** capture it for any screen recording. Choose **Animated cursor** or **Hide cursor** before recording if you also want to restyle the pointer later. **Show cursor** bakes the pointer into the video, but zooms still work.
- The **Tella Chrome extension** captures it when you share a browser tab. Sharing a window or your whole screen doesn't include cursor data.
- **Uploaded videos** and camera-only clips don't have it. You can add zooms to an uploaded screen recording by hand (see below), but not generate them.


For demos, use the desktop apps. They record up to 4K, capture system audio, and always include cursor data.


## Step 1: Record as normal


Click through what you're demonstrating at a normal pace. Don't slow down or hover to "help" the zooms; the algorithm keys off real clicks, and unnatural pauses produce zooms with nothing in them.


Two habits that improve the generated zooms:


1. **Click where you want the viewer to look.** A click is the strongest signal Auto Zoom has. If you talk about a setting without clicking it, the zoom may stay on your last click.
2. **Park the cursor while you talk.** Wandering the pointer around creates jittery targets.


## Step 2: Generate zooms


1. Open the recording in the editor.
2. Click **Effect** in the sidebar, or press` E` . The Effect timeline shows zoom, blur, and highlight cards above the transcript.
3. Under **Zooms** , click **Generate zooms** (the sparkles icon).
4. Choose a **Style** :


- **Adaptive** (default) follows your clicks and adjusts depth to the amount of activity.
- **Subtle** : fewer, shallower, longer zooms. Good for lectures and long tutorials.
- **Moderate** : between Subtle and Intense.
- **Intense** : more frequent, deeper, shorter zooms. Good for short social demos.


5. Click **Generate** .


The menu stays open while you compare styles. Tella remembers the last style you chose and uses it next time.


Scrub through the result once. Expect a handful of zooms you'd keep, a couple to nudge, and maybe one to delete.


## Step 3: Fix the ones you don't agree with


Generated zooms are ordinary zooms, so everything here works on both.


**Move or resize:** drag a zoom card along the Effect timeline to move it, or drag either edge to change its duration. The preview follows the edge you're dragging while the playhead stays put.


**Change the target or depth:** select the card and choose a **Mode** :


- **Manual** locks onto a fixed point. Drag the **Target** on the canvas, then set **Scale** (100% to 350%). Hold **Cmd** (Mac) or **Ctrl** (Windows) while dragging to keep the target on a horizontal or vertical line.
- **Auto** follows the recorded cursor for the length of the zoom.


**Delete:** select the card and press **Delete** or **Backspace** . To start over, open **More actions** and choose **Reset all zooms** .


**Split:** put the playhead inside a zoom and press` X` . Both halves keep the original mode, target, and scale, which is the quickest way to retarget the second half of a long zoom.


**Pan instead of zooming out:** place two zooms directly beside each other and Tella pans between the targets without zooming out in between. Drag the shared seam to move the boundary.


**Add one Auto Zoom missed:** drag across a range on the timeline (or across words in the transcript) and press` Z` . With nothing selected, **Add zoom** creates a zoom of up to five seconds from the playhead.


Zooms snap to transcript word boundaries and other zoom edges. Hold **Option** (Mac) or **Alt** (Windows) to drag freely.


## Step 4: Motion blur, animation style, and camera shrink


1. **Motion blur.** Under **Zooms** , expand **Advanced zoom settings** , turn on **Motion blur** , and drag the slider between **Subtle** and **Strong** . It softens the fast part of every zoom and pan, and the cursor if you use the animated cursor. About a third of the way along is a good start.
2. **Animation style.** Open **Layout** , click **Layout settings** , and under **Animation** choose **Gentle** , **Moderate** , or **Snappy** . Gentle suits tutorials; Snappy suits 30-second product clips. The style applies to zooms and layout changes together.
3. **Shrink camera during zooms.** If you have a camera bubble, turn this on in **Advanced zoom settings** . The bubble shrinks while a zoom plays and returns to size when it ends, so it doesn't cover the detail.


All three apply to the whole video by default. Turn on **Adjust this clip** if you want a different setting on one clip.


## Step 5: Share


Click **Share** in the top right, then **Copy link** . Tella hosts the video and the zooms play in the hosted version, so there's no export or render to wait for. If you need a file for YouTube or a course platform, export an MP4 in up to 4K.


## Auto-apply zooms to every recording


To skip the Effect panel entirely:


1. Click your avatar and open **Settings** .
2. Go to **Preferences** under **Account** .
3. Under **Recording** , turn on **Auto-apply zooms** .


Tella adds zooms as soon as the recording's uploads finish, using the last style you picked (Adaptive if you've never chosen one). You can still open the editor and adjust them.


## Zooms on a video recorded somewhere else


Upload the MP4 to Tella and add zooms by hand:


1. Select the range you want zoomed on the timeline.
2. Press` Z` .
3. Set **Mode** to **Manual** , drag the **Target** , and choose a **Scale** .


Hold **Shift** while dragging to select several ranges and create a zoom for each at once. Copy and paste ( **Cmd/Ctrl + C** , **Cmd/Ctrl + V** ) carries mode, target, scale, and duration between videos.


## Common mistakes


- **Zooming too far.** A 350% zoom into a 1080p recording gets soft. Use the lowest scale that makes the detail readable, and record in 4K on the desktop apps if you know you'll zoom a lot.
- **Intense style on a long tutorial.** It's tiring to watch. Use Subtle or Adaptive for anything over a few minutes.
- **A zoom that outlives its dialog.** Trim the zoom's end to the moment the action finishes; the word markers on the Effect timeline make it easy to line up with your narration.
- **Zooms that cut off mid-sentence.** Zooms snap to transcript words, so drag the edge to the end of the sentence you're saying about that area.
